To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
resveratol suppresses EGF-dependent Erk1/Erk2 activation in human prostate cancer cells in vitro and that the phytochemical does so by selectively antagonizing PKCα activation.
the phytochemical resvertatrol suppresses EGFR-dependent Erk 1/2 activation in human androgen-independent prostate carcinoma cells by selectively inhibiting the isozyme PKCα.
the phytochemical resv antagonizes EGF-dependent Erk1/ 2 activation in human androgen-independent prostate cells with associated isozyme-selectiv PKCα inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with

defining the mechanisms of resveratol-induced suppression of EGFR-dependent Erk signaling in PC-3 human prostate cancer cells and with identifying the cellular PKC isoenzyme(s) that is selectively inhibited by resveratrol.
the molecular mechanisms by which resveratrol antagonizes the EGFR-activated Erk1/2 signaling pathway in human prostate cancer cells.
the molecular mechanisms by which the dietary phytoestrogen resveratrol inhibits the growth and metastatic progression of human androgen-independent prostate carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
resveratol inhibits PKCα and that this inhibition results in the abrogation of TPA-induced EGFR-dependent Erk activation.

resveratol antagonizes EGF-dependent Erk1/ 2 activation in human AI PrC cells with isozyme selective PKCα inhibition, and that the effects are mediated by the ability of the phytochemical to inhibit the PKCα isoform.
resveratol has a growth inhibitory effect on prostate cancer cells and this effect is due to the inhibition of the EGFR/ERK1/2 pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
resveratol is an effective inhibitor of EGFR-dependent Erk activation and that this effect correlates with isozymes selective inhibition of PKCα.
resveratol is a PKC inhibitor that suppresses EGFR-dependent Erk activation in AI PrCa cells.
the phytochemical resv. antagonizes EGF/TGFα/Erk1/2 activation in human AI Prca cells by isozyme-selectively inhibiting PKCα.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we found that resveratol inhibits a key survival pathway (EGFR/Erk1/2) in human prostate cancer cells.
resveratol is an isozyme-selectively PKCα inhibitor in human prostate cancer cells, and this may have therapeutic value.
resveratol can inhibit the growth of prostate cancer cells in vitro and in vivo.
